entries.1a588391098f0052: The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] states that the company's corporate group consists of 19 subsidiaries, and that its main businesses are manufacture, sale and rental of temporary construction equipment, manufacture and sale of aluminum products for housing and construction sites and fitness equipment, and manufacture and sale of electronic products, while it also carries out business activities such as logistics, research and other services related to each business. The core business is the sale and rental of temporary equipment; by strengthening collaboration between the two, the company is working to expand market share for the new scaffold “Albatross” and other high value-added products. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥62,632 million (up 1.7% year on year), marking a record high for the second consecutive year.
entries.1a89b2f89e67c911: Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 (excluding intersegment internal revenue) was ¥24,674 million for the Construction Equipment-Related Business (up 0.4% year on year), ¥17,881 million for the Rental-Related Business (down 0.7% year on year), ¥14,456 million for the Housing Equipment-Related Business (up 3.5% year on year) and ¥5,620 million for the Electronic Equipment-Related Business (up 11.0% year on year), for a total of ¥62,632 million. In the Electronic Equipment-Related Business, replacement demand for digitalized fire-service radios led the increase in revenue, with fire-service radios up 145.9% year on year.

entries.1c2c4b475e50e402: The fiscal year-end is March 20 each year, and the current fiscal year runs from March 21, 2025 to March 20, 2026. As of March 20, 2026, the number of consolidated employees was 1,471 (194 temporary employees are excluded from this figure). There are four reportable segments: the Construction Equipment-Related Business, the Rental-Related Business, the Housing Equipment-Related Business and the Electronic Equipment-Related Business, and there is no parent company or other entity. The annual securities report states that the company is working to execute the “Medium-Term Management Plan 2027” (the three years from the fiscal year ended March 2025 to the fiscal year ending March 2027), and that the numerical targets of this plan were revised as of May 1, 2026.

entries.2c5ecc346cd143f6: A reportable segment that makes, or purchases, and sells ladders and stepladders, aluminum profiles and resin molding materials, stationary lift work platforms, surveying instruments and laser equipment, aluminum bridges, various carts and folding handcarts, and fitness-related products. Net sales for the fiscal year ended March 2026 (excluding internal sales between segments) were ¥14,456 million (up 3.5% year on year), and the segment loss was ¥363 million (an improvement of ¥160 million from the previous year). ALINCO INCORPORATED sells products made by Suzhou ALINCO Metal Products Co., Ltd.; in addition, Hikari Mold Co., Ltd. manufactures and sells aluminum profiles and resin molding materials, Cip Co., Ltd. manufactures and sells stationary lift work platforms, S.T.S. Co., Ltd. manufactures and sells surveying instruments and other products, and Showa Bridge Sales Co., Ltd. manufactures and sells aluminum bridges and other products. The securities report states that sales of aerial work platforms for sales channels such as construction equipment rental, and of brown rice cold storage units due to farmers' and others' needs to stockpile rice for their own use amid soaring rice prices, were strong, while for fitness-related products, new products were launched but the recovery of consumer sentiment was weak, so net sales were flat from the previous year.

entries.35402110ab312ee4: A reportable segment that rents temporary equipment for mid- and high-rise and low-rise construction, and temporary spectator stands, and it also carries out scaffolding installation. Net sales for the fiscal year ended March 2026 (excluding internal sales between segments) were ¥17,881 million (down 0.7% year on year), and segment profit was ¥1,269 million (down 9.8% year on year). ALINCO INCORPORATED rents some of the products it makes to customers as its own operating assets; in addition, Oriental Kizai Co., Ltd. also carries out rentals, and Tokyo Kasetsu Built Co., Ltd. (renamed ALINCO Building Tech Co., Ltd. as of March 21, 2026) carries out scaffolding construction work. In Thailand, ALINCO SCAFFOLDING (THAILAND) CO.,LTD., and in Indonesia, PT. ALINCO SCAFFOLDING INDONESIA, operate the rental business. The securities report states that profit decreased because of increased depreciation, as investment in rental assets continued in response to the trend "from purchase to rental." Investment in rental assets for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,738 million.

entries.56e2c088091f769c: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥2,212 million (up 0.8% year on year), ordinary profit was ¥2,777 million (up 3.7% year on year), and profit attributable to owners of parent was ¥1,753 million (down 10.5% year on year). Ordinary profit increased due to foreign exchange gains from the valuation of foreign currency-denominated assets, while profit attributable to owners of parent decreased because extraordinary gains declined. Operating profit was 28.6% below the fiscal year ended March 2026 plan of ¥3,100 million. The annual securities report attributes this to slow growth in profit margins due to product mix and increased depreciation expenses, rising purchasing costs due to the weaker yen, and delays in progress on expanding production capacity in the Electronic Equipment-Related Business. Most overseas contract manufacturing transactions are denominated in U.S. dollars, and to stabilize purchasing costs, foreign exchange hedges are carried out through forward foreign exchange contracts.

entries.74b8deaac9793439: A reportable segment that manufactures and sells temporary construction equipment (scaffolding and more) and logistics storage equipment, and it has the largest net sales of the 4 reportable segments. Net sales for the fiscal year ended March 2026 (excluding internal sales between segments) were ¥24,674 million (up 0.4% year on year), and segment profit was ¥1,971 million (down 10.9% year on year). The main product is the new scaffolding "Albatross." ALINCO INCORPORATED manufactures and sells, or purchases and sells, mainly to customers in Japan; in addition, Oriental Kizai Co., Ltd. sells the Company's products, Sofuku Kouki Co., Ltd. handles logistics storage equipment (racks) and steel flooring, and Uekin Co., Ltd. carries out the design and manufacture of metal dies and metal press processing. Products manufactured by Suzhou ALINCO Metal Products Co., Ltd. and ALINCO (THAILAND) CO.,LTD. are sold in Japan, China, Thailand, Indonesia and elsewhere. The securities report states that although the shift of temporary equipment "from purchase to rental" continued, construction demand was firm, and sales increased centered on "Albatross," but profit decreased because sales were dominated by relatively low-margin products such as heavily worn scaffolding planks.
entries.79dcb91841fc1956: A reportable segment that makes and sells wireless communication equipment and printed circuit boards, and it has the smallest net sales of the 4 reportable segments. Net sales for the fiscal year ended March 2026 (excluding internal sales between segments) were ¥5,620 million (up 11.0% year on year), and the segment loss was ¥441 million (an improvement of ¥93 million from the previous year). ALINCO INCORPORATED manufactures and sells wireless communication equipment mainly to customers in Japan and overseas, and ALINCO Toyama Co., Ltd. also carries out manufacturing and sales. The design, manufacture and sale of printed circuit boards are carried out by Higashi Denshi Kogyo Co., Ltd. (renamed ALINCO E-Tech Co., Ltd. as of March 21, 2026). The securities report states that, driven by replacement demand for fire department radios that were digitized with a deadline of end of May 2016, fire department radios rose 145.9% year on year and led the increase in sales, while a loss resulted because capacity expansion was delayed in the subsidiary's printed circuit board business.
